title: orion180 insurance targets 17 billion valuation us ipo 2026 09 09
text:
Sept 9 (Reuters) - Orion180 Insurance said on Wednesday it was targeting a valuation of up to $1.68 billion in its U.S. ​initial public offering, as the fall IPO window gains momentum.
The Melbourne, ‌Florida-based firm is seeking up to $340 million by offering 20 million shares priced between $15 and $17 apiece.
The listing comes as the IPO market shakes off its summer lull and ​dealmakers rush to bring offerings to capitalize on the post-Labor Day ​fall window, traditionally one of the busiest for new deals.
"We're currently ⁠expecting a busy fall," said Nicholas Einhorn, vice president, research, at Renaissance ​Capital, a provider of IPO-focused research and ETFs, adding the strong performance of ​the Renaissance IPO index this year suggests solid demand for new stocks.
Holtec Nuclear and American Savings Bank launched their U.S. IPO roadshows on Tuesday, kicking off the fall listing ​window.
The insurance pipeline is also gaining momentum, with Bamboo Insurance filing for a ​U.S. IPO last month.
"Insurance has been a quiet sector in the IPO market so far ‌this ⁠year, but we did see a wave of homeowners' insurers coming public last year," Einhorn said, noting the successful listings of American Integrity (AII.N)

"A relatively benign hurricane season so far this year has ​probably helped these stocks ​and is encouraging ⁠Orion180, which is mostly Southeast-focused, to come public now."
Founded in 2018 by Kenneth Gregg, Orion180 provides excess and surplus ​lines homeowners insurance across 14 U.S. states. Its key ​markets include ⁠Texas, California, and Florida.
The firm currently focuses on homeowners and residential flood insurance markets, generating roughly $601 million of managed premiums written in the last 12 months ⁠ended ​June 30, according to the filing.
RBC Capital Markets, ​UBS Investment Bank and Raymond James are lead book-running managers. Orion180 will list on the Nasdaq ​under the symbol "OIG".
